motion.name: atom-pulse

motion.purpose: Plays on every atom activation except the silent initial C2; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: print-sequence
motion.value: html.print set in head unless reduced motion, removed after 2600ms
motion.purpose: Hero only, once per load: label clip-reveal 700ms; strip scaleX 620ms@120ms, fields 420/500/580ms; name clip press-up 640ms@300ms; role 480ms@520ms; spec rows clip-draw 520ms from 620ms, 60ms stagger; actions 480ms@880ms; molecule plate reveal 760ms@200ms; bonds stroke-dashoffset from C2 in BFS order (700ms start, 120ms per hop, 380ms each); heteroatoms fade 300ms; annotation pins ~1.3s; then C2 pulses. Never replays on other sections.

motion.name: paper-stack
motion.value: html.stack added by script after measuring, never under reduced motion; main>section sticky at --stick = min(bar height, viewport - section height); --cover (0..1) = (viewport - next sheet top) / (viewport - bar), rAF-throttled on scroll; covered label transform: scale(1 - 0.05*cover) translateY(-14px*cover) from its top edge, filter: brightness(1 - 0.3*cover)
motion.purpose: The one scroll-linked motion: each section sticks and the next slides over it while the covered label sinks and dims. Anchor clicks and deep links scroll to flow position. The nav current marker is the last section whose top has passed mid-viewport.

focus.purpose: Global focus-visible ring; turns white inside cobalt rows and the contact label; atoms use a 2px white ring at 15px radius.

groundGradient.purpose: Pale lab-bench page ground with one soft vertical highlight; repainted by every section in the paper stack so it covers the sheet beneath. Flat fallback #d6d4cd.

themeColor.purpose: Browser chrome matches the label-stock top bar.

narrative.overview:
Every section of the CV is a paper label laid on a lab bench. The page ground is the bench: a pale warm grey with one soft vertical highlight down the middle of the viewport, fixed while the labels scroll past. The labels stack like sheets of paper: each section sticks in place and the next slides up over it, the covered label sinking slightly and dimming as it is buried. On the bench sit near-white label panels divided by black rules into the grids a supplier catalogue uses: specification rows, slotted entries, a certificate-of-analysis table, a reference list.

Cobalt is printed boldly, as a supplier prints its house colour. Each label opens with a solid cobalt slab, the 18px band fused with the head, carrying the section headline in white. The hero lot strip, the molecule plate, catalogue numbers, the prize-winning talk and the whole contact label are cobalt; everything else on the label stays ink on stock. The type is industrial and compressed: names and section titles in a heavy condensed grotesk in capitals, running text in the same family at normal width, mono only where a catalogue would print a number, value or date. Corners are square everywhere. Depth is a single soft drop under each label, as if lifted a millimetre off the bench, plus a short upward shadow where an incoming sheet overlaps the one beneath.

The live element is the molecule on the hero's cobalt plate: a white skeletal aspirin whose carbons, on hover or focus, pin a leader-line annotation with an illustrative shift, while bonds one and two hops away brighten and pulse outward like message passing. On first load the hero label prints itself once. The paper stack is the one deliberate scroll-linked motion; nothing else animates on arrival or on scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Pale lab-bench ground, white label stock, black rules, one bold cobalt printed as solid slabs and chips.
Condensed heavy capitals for names; mono only for numbers, values and dates.
Fixed-slot entries with right-aligned, deep-linkable cobalt catalogue chips.
Square corners and a 2px / 1px / hairline rule hierarchy instead of cards.
One signature interaction (atom annotation with message-passing pulse), one once-per-load print sequence on the hero, and one scroll-linked paper stack.

rules.name: The One Printed Colour Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only chromatic colour on a label. Use it boldly as solid slabs, plates, chips and rows with white on top, never as a second tint, gradient or outline-only accent. Everything else on stock is ink, soft ink or hairline.

rules.name: The Three Substrates Rule
rules.body: Text sits on label stock or the bench (ink family, with deep cobalt ink for hover and current state), or on cobalt (on-band family). Never set ink on cobalt at rest, or cobalt-coloured text on cobalt.

rules.name: The Black Alpha Rule
rules.body: Translucent rules and shadows are pure black at one of four fixed alphas (12%, 30%, 35%, 55%). No tinted shadows, no warm or cobalt alpha.

rules.name: The Width-Is-Rank Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by width and weight of one family, not by adding families. Narrower and heavier means more of a name; 100% width means prose.

rules.name: The Printer Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a catalogue would print from a database: numbers, codes, dates, identifiers, stack lists. Never for headings or descriptive sentences.

rules.name: The Equal Edge Rule
rules.body: Every label sits inside the same edge on left and right at every width; nothing bleeds to the viewport edge except the bench and the bar.

rules.name: The Paper On Bench Rule
rules.body: The label is the only thing that floats at rest. Everything inside it, cobalt included, is printed flat; lift appears only as a response to pointer hover. The stack's sinking and dimming act on the whole label, never on parts of it.

rules.name: The Rule Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: 2px ink closes a group, 1px ink separates peers, 1px hairline separates attributes inside one entry. Never use a radius or a tinted card to do a rule's job.

rules.name: The Slab Rule
rules.body: Cobalt arrives as a full-bleed slab, plate, chip or row with square edges and white on top, closed by a 2px ink rule where it meets stock.

rules.name: The Once Rule
rules.body: Arrival motion happens once, on the hero, on load; it never replays on other sections.

rules.name: The One Scroll Rule
rules.body: The paper stack is the only scroll-linked motion. No reveal-on-scroll, parallax or scroll-triggered entrances anywhere else; every other motion is a response to the visitor.

dos: **Do** open every section with a label whose head is a solid cobalt slab: white headline, mist mono metadata on its baseline, closed by a 2px ink rule.
**Do** give every new piece of work an entry with the fixed slots and a unique, linkable cobalt catalogue chip right-aligned on the title baseline.
**Do** separate content with the 2px / 1px / hairline rule hierarchy rather than boxes or tinted fills.
**Do** print cobalt boldly as slabs, plates, chips and rows with white (on-band) text and mist (on-band-2) secondary text.
**Do** keep corners square (0px) on every element, including images, chips and buttons.
**Do** use the single house ease, keep hover lifts at 1–2px with a soft shadow, and keep arrival motion to the hero's one print sequence.
**Do** give any new section the paper-stack behaviour by making it a direct child section of main, with the bench gradient behind its label.
**Do** draw translucent rules and shadows in black at the four recorded alphas.
donts: **Don't** round corners or turn entries into floating cards with their own shadows; only the label floats.
**Don't** add a second accent colour, tint cobalt into gradients, or use tinted (warm or cobalt) shadows and rules.
**Don't** set headings or descriptive sentences in mono.
**Don't** add hard offset shadows or glows.
**Don't** put a small caps line above a section headline; the label head's metadata sits beside the headline, on its baseline.
**Don't** add scroll-linked motion beyond the paper stack, or replay the print sequence on other sections.
